name: Jellyfin Federation
description: Aggregate content from multiple Jellyfin servers into unified virtual libraries
overview: The Jellyfin Federation Plugin allows you to create a unified media library by aggregating content from multiple remote Jellyfin servers. Stream content from any server without file synchronization.
changelog: Fixes a data-loss bug introduced in 0.0.42. That release added a check that a remote is actually running Federation before syncing from it, and deletes a server's entire federated library when it decides the plugin is gone. The check treated *any* unsuccessful probe as "plugin uninstalled" - including a timeout, a refused connection, or a 502/503 from a Cloudflare Tunnel or reverse proxy in front of a briefly-down origin. A tunnel hiccup lasting seconds would therefore have wiped every federated movie and episode from that server, exactly the outcome the surrounding code's own comment claimed it avoided, and a 502 outage of precisely that kind was observed on this setup the same day. The probe is now tri-state: a remote is only treated as having removed the plugin when it 404s this plugin's route *and* separately answers System/Info/Public, proving the address is a live Jellyfin rather than a misrouted tunnel that 404s everything. Anything unverifiable - unreachable, 5xx, or an access gate answering 401/403 - is now an ordinary transient failure that leaves cached content untouched, the same as every other sync failure. Four regression tests pin the specific failure modes (502, unreachable, 404-everything, 403), each verified to fail against the old behaviour. The probe result is also cached briefly per server, so a sync spanning several libraries costs one round trip instead of one per library.
